A recap of the first week of my second semester.

## Monday

I was really nervous before my first class. I had a really bad stomach ache, but it eventually went away. It happens every morning before school, and it's really annoying, but i have to bear with it.

My first class was ELEG305 and I feel super under prepared for it. I'm actually not really supposed to be taking it (it's a sophomore class, and it had a prerequisite before this year), but I plan on graduating in 3 years. We'll see how it goes though. The content seems really interesting, but I hope it isn't too difficult.

After the class, I went to pick up my brother from school.[^1]

[^1]: His school is only 5 minutes or so away, so it's really convenient.

I had breakfast at 12 (unhealthy, I know), and then I worked on an assignment for CISC210.

I then had my Honors Colloquium course, which seems really interesting! The professor seems really nice, although he's rather unfiltered in his language.

## Tuesday

It was super cold today. After dropping off my brother, I went to Gore Hall and stayed there for around three hours working on a few assignments. I saw a some friends passing through there (Raima, Ellie, and Blessed)!

I spent an awful amount of time trying to install a Jupyter Notebook with a C++ kernel (I'll be using this for notes), and it took a while, but it finally worked.

Then I had my Systems Programming class. I have professor Nazim from my CS1 class again, so that's nice to see. We just went over the Syllabus and talked about some random things.

Apparently, the labs are optional, so I'll likely won't show up to any of them. I went with Joshua and Ryan, and there were only 5 or so people there when we showed up. I guess professor Nazim shouldn't have said that the labs are optional...

I went to the library and read 'A Good Man is Hard to Find' for my honors colloquium, and I'll have a whole separate post (link post) detailing my thoughts toward it. Spoiler warning: my interpretation is quite deranged, but it's all I have and I think I have a pretty good argument for it.

I then had my Engineering Math class, and I think I'll like this class as well. The professor is in a way, brimming with energy, and he's really passionate about math. We learned about the classification of differential equations towards the end of the class.

Finally, it was time for my Digital Systems class. I'm not very sure what to think about it yet, partly because I was busy figuring out how I would organize my notes for my classes. I still haven't really decided.

Anyways, there wasn't much to today. I saw a few old friends from high school, and I rode the bus with Avneet towards the parking spaces. He mentioned the Winter Fellows program he took part of, which i found really interesting. Maybe I'll apply for the Summer Fellows program if I can.

## Wednesday

I feel even more unprepared for my Signals and Systems class. I've found that the way Dr. Brockmeier teaches the class is far from my liking. To me, he seems to be introducing concepts as he likes and it doesn't feel structured at all. I think I might just read the book because I left class more confused, and we're just starting!

After class, I stayed in my car for a while rewriting notes. Things make SO much more sense now.

My physics lab isn't starting until next week, so I don't have to worry about that for now.

After picking up my brother from school, I went home and came back to campus around 2:30. My colloquium class was really interesting today! Unfortunately, we didn't discuss *our* interpretation of the reading, but we had some very interesting conversations about who's actually right when it comes to interpreting a text: the author, or the reader? In my opinion, authors and readers can interpret a text incorrectly. So then what decides the meaning of a text?

His view is that the words themselves is what matters. The meaning of a text doesn't change with time or the condition of society.

I agree with his view, and I wonder where this class is going to go. We have been assigned 46 pages to read, and that might not sound like a lot, but we'll be discussing on Friday and I haven't started reading yet...

I've gotta get to reading then.

## Thursday

I've barely read the book and it's due tomorrow... how annoying. I really didn't feel up to doing anything at all today.

My Systems Programming class was really boring. I wonder if it'll be anything like CS1. Honestly, we didn't really do much of anything. I just have to give it time, I guess. it's only the second day after all.

Afterwards I spent a little time reading and then I had my math class. I was really lost today. I didn't really understand Dr. Schreffler when he started talking about singular solutions of ODE's and Existence & Uniqueness. Everyone else seemed to grasp things just fine, however. 

He seems to just introduce things out of nowhere, providing no sort of motivation. Maybe it's just me though. 

I then had my Digital Systems class. Things were slightly better, but I felt as if the professor was going through the slides rather quickly. I felt really slow. 

I know I'm not very smart, but these classes are suddenly so overwhelming to me. 

Things really aren't going so well, and it's going to be really hard to catch up.

## Friday

My ELEG305 discussion went well today. I actually understood the problems, but then again, they were fairly basic. We started the homework, which I'm really thankful for because I haven't started it myself.

I then had a giant 4 hour block. I went home to eat and finish reading my assigned reading. It turns out that we didn't really have to read all of it, but we still had a fairly interesting dicussion. I missed a few points Scalia (the author) made, probably because I didn't take notes. I might have to reread it, since it seems like we'll be spending a while studying his points in depth.

I haven't really done much today. I should probably get some work done, but I am so lazy.

## Note
I probably won't continue with weekly posts like this. I already have a private diary to maintain, so if anything, this will feel like an extra chore.
